free_tier.stated: Hobby: 200 CPU minutes a month included; a CPU minute is one CPU running for one minute. Pro: USD 0.0035 per CPU minute. Beta on all plans
free_tier.notes: the true unit is CPU minutes (CPUs multiplied by task run time, rounded up to the second, 1 second minimum); the vocabulary has no core-minutes term, so unit is minutes. Each run spends 4 CPUs on bootstrapping and 2 CPUs by default on each task that runs; cached and skipped tasks cost nothing

per_object_cap.stated: 2 CPUs and 4 GB of memory per task by default, up to 32 CPUs and 64 GB of memory with a ci:cpus tag; bootstrapping install step 4 CPUs and 8 GB by default. Job time limit: unverified: no Vercel CI page states a task or run time limit

retention.stated: unverified: no Vercel CI page states how long runs and task logs are kept

egress.terms: unverified: no Vercel CI page states a network egress policy for tasks; the network traffic of tasks passes through a Vercel CI certificate authority

interface_detail: a git push to a GitHub repository connected to a Vercel project runs every task tagged ci in turbo.json; a repository is enabled with the vercel ci enable command, runs and task logs are read in the dashboard CI tab, with the vercel ci CLI, the Vercel MCP and the REST API, and the status of the tasks is posted to the pull request as a check
tooling: Turborepo 2.11.7 or later and Vercel CLI 64.3.1 or later; tasks run in Linux containers on x86_64, Amazon Linux 2023 by default or Ubuntu 24.04 with a ci:os:ubuntu tag, with Node.js 24, git, Docker and common build tools preinstalled; extra tools are installed during bootstrapping with an install command in vercel.json
chaining: a hosted runner for tagged Turborepo tasks (lint, type check, tests, builds) triggered only by a git push to a private GitHub repository; it has no schedule, manual or pull-request trigger and no public-repository support, so GitHub Actions on a public repository and the other hosted runners of this topic come first for general jobs
